jp: 食卓[しょくたく]の向[む]かいで母[はは]が何[なに]か読[よ]んでいます。「お母[かあ]さん、{それ|ko-kore}は新聞[しんぶん]?」と聞[き]きました。
en: My mother across the dining table is reading something. I asked, 'Mom, is that a newspaper?'
why: The thing is near the listener, my mother, so it is それ.

jp: 朝[あさ]、家[いえ]を出[で]る前[まえ]に、手[て]に持[も]ったお弁当[べんとう]を見[み]せて、「{これ|ko-kore}は妹[いもうと]が作[つく]りました」と言[い]いました。
en: In the morning before leaving the house, I showed the lunchbox in my hand and said, 'My younger sister made this.'
why: The lunchbox is in the speaker's hand, so it is close to the speaker: これ.

jp: 夕方[ゆうがた]、父[ちち]と庭[にわ]に出[で]ると、遠[とお]くの空[そら]に赤[あか]いものが見[み]えました。「お父[とう]さん、{あれ|ko-kore}は何[なん]？」と聞[き]きました。
en: In the evening I went out into the garden with my father, and I could see something red in the faraway sky. 'Dad, what is that?'
why: The thing is far from both speaker and listener, so it is あれ.

jp: 母[はは]が「今夜[こんや]は友達[ともだち]の家[いえ]に泊[と]まるわ」と言[い]ったので、「{それ|ko-kore}は聞[き]いていないよ」と答[こた]えました。
en: My mother said, 'I'm staying at a friend's house tonight,' so I answered, 'I haven't heard about that.'
why: Something the other person has just said is referred to with それ.
